ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single-loop circuit: on the left is a 10 V voltage source, with the upper terminal marked positive and the lower terminal marked negative; a 1 kΩ resistor is connected in series above; on the right is a diode, the reference direction of current i is downward along the right branch, and the diode voltage v is marked with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative. Reasoning: According to the given diode characteristics, if it is assumed that the diode is cut off, then i=0 and the resistor voltage drop is 0, so the voltage across the diode will equal the source voltage v=10 V, which does not satisfy the cutoff condition v<0.7 V, so the diode cannot be cut off and must operate in the conduction segment. When conducting, i=(v-0.7)/500, that is, v=0.7+500i. Write KVL for the single loop: 10=1000i+v. Substitution gives 10=1000i+0.7+500i, so 9.3=1500i, i=0.0062 A=6.2 mA.
